originality.rationale: Actual semantic record searches and own-current-week overlap comparison found no exact or dominating arclength-hypocycloid tail theorem. Closest full published texts concern polygonal interior-area Poisson deficits or a polygon-to-circle boundary-arclength crossover; neither entails fixed integer-cusp hypocycloid boundary sampling. The full 2015 hypocycloid construction text has a different question. Historical priority remains provisional. Wei Lao (2010) Chapter 5, Theorems 5.1 and 5.3, was inspected in full PDF at the relevant theorem pages and confirmed to treat straight polygon edges with distinct adjacent-ray coefficients, not the fixed curved-cusp arclength law. A recoverable older endpoint-cusp arc claim was compared at the hypothesis level: its cusp tangent is transverse to the diametral chord and has a distinct four-thirds tail exponent, whereas hypocycloid cusps are longitudinal and yield a quadratic tail.
residual_risks: An unindexed older theorem on random hypocycloid chords or singular arclength boundary extremes might overlap.
The 2009 cycloidal-areas article full text could not be inspected, only repository abstract/metadata; no whole-document noncoverage assertion is made.
Semantic search nonretrieval alone is never a novelty certificate.

Wei Lao (2010) supplies a closely related exponential point-process methodology for polygon perimeters, which this theorem specializes in spirit but not by an object-preserving parameter substitution; future broader general theorems under different curvature singularity assumptions may imply the present statement.
